note: ENUMERATED DELIBERATE STRICTNESS. Every entry is a case where the typed schema at the integration layer REJECTS an input that the engine's own argument surface would accept. That direction is safe by construction: soundness forbids the opposite, where the engine accepts something the schema refuses. The parity suite requires SET EQUALITY against this file, so a new divergence and a dead entry both fail it. The diff of this file IS the audit trail of the decision to allow one.
key_scheme: `members` are classes, not fixture ids: `<kind>/<mutation>` for the kind-matrix and mutation families (the same pair appears in hundreds of cases), the id itself for the pointer/formula families, and `<family>/<fn>` for spec-accept/optional-omitted.

divergences.reason: an explicit JSON null on an OPTIONAL argument
divergences.rationale: adapt_args (adapters line 180) reads an explicit null as ABSENT (`!is.null(raw[[nm]])`), so it accepts it silently. The Zod schema is `.optional()` — NEVER `.nullable()` — and rejects it. Deliberate: 'null means absent' is a trap for model output (and on a required argument it becomes a 422 later); the worker omits the key instead. ⚠️ THE `members` LIST IS A SAMPLE, NOT A DEFINITION: a `<kind>/null` appears here only when the corpus HAPPENS to draw the (kind, null) pair on an OPTIONAL argument — in the kind-matrix that depends on whether the kind's representative has that argument optional, and in the `mutation` family on the `sample.int` draw inside the corpus exporter. REVISION 2026-08-05: `arw_write_parquet` lost an argument (3->2, `sink` became `export=`) and sits at index 4/914, so the `mutation` family's RNG stream shifted and roughly 909 pairs were re-drawn. Measured result: `df_handle/null`, `matrix_handle/null` and `raw/null` LEFT (no node now draws `null` on an optional argument of those kinds; their kind-matrix representatives — arw_write_parquet/x, bn_apply/x, shape_fillna/replace — are REQUIRED, so the validation schema rejects and the case is P2, not P3), and `int_array/null` ARRIVED (mutate/gts_ar_x/ar/null). The MECHANISM and the DIRECTION of the class did not change — which is why this stays ONE entry with its original `since` rather than splitting into a second. NOTE on the `path` kind: `path/null` does NOT belong here — its representative (arw_open_dataset/sources) is REQUIRED, the validation schema rejects with `missing-required`, and Zod agrees (P2). No `path/*` is a divergence: all 11 invalid mutations in the matrix are rejected by BOTH sides. REVISION 2026-08-07: the node `mfl_ts_from_rdb` was deleted (914->913) and two others renamed, so the `mutation` family's RNG stream SHIFTED AGAIN (252 ids left, 247 arrived). Measured result, exactly the inverse of the previous revision: `raw_handle/null` LEFT, and `df_handle/null` and `matrix_handle/null` ARRIVED. The MECHANISM and the DIRECTION did not change — no new semantics, so the entry stays as ONE with its original `since`.

divergences.reason: the frozen contract's integer coercion accepts anything, often yielding a silent missing value
divergences.rationale: The string "42" becomes 42, "abc" becomes a missing value with a warning, 1e18 overflows to a missing value, and a one-element list collapses to 1. The typed schema requires a genuine JSON integer. Typed edges plus typed forms: the worker always sends a number, and a missing value that reaches a wrapper gate is an expensive, late 422.

divergences.reason: the frozen contract's numeric coercion accepts anything
divergences.rationale: The string "0.5" becomes 0.5, "abc" becomes a missing value with a warning, and a list is flattened. Same reasoning as integer.

divergences.reason: the frozen contract's boolean coercion accepts anything
divergences.rationale: "TRUE" becomes true, "yes" becomes a missing value, 1 becomes true, and a list is coerced too. A silent missing value in a boolean flag changes THE MEANING of the method — the typed schema requires an explicit JSON boolean.

divergences.reason: the frozen contract's string coercion accepts anything
divergences.rationale: A large float, a one-element list and so on all yield a string. The typed schema requires a JSON string.

divergences.reason: membership is NOT checked by adapt_args
divergences.rationale: The frozen contract's coercion step CONVERTS ONLY THE TYPE for kind='enum' and NEVER checks membership; the membership check lives INSIDE the wrapper, OUTSIDE the modelled class (which is why the reason code 'enum-invalid' is NEVER produced by the engine). The typed schema checks the enum up front. UPDATE: the type conversion is now type-aware — numeric when the spec's values are numeric, textual otherwise — no longer textual in every case. For the engine's ONLY numeric enum (des_decompose.order_poly, whose values are 1 and 3) the engine now accepts BOTH "3" AND 3, whereas the typed schema — which serialises enum members to strings — accepts only "3". The typed schema remains STRICTER, so the class stays P1-safe and its direction is unchanged.

divergences.reason: flattening accepts a scalar, and an empty vector passes
divergences.rationale: A bare 3 is flattened to a one-element vector, and an empty list flattens to an empty vector. The typed schema requires an array of at least one element: an array socket means an array socket, and an empty vector almost always breaks later at a wrapper gate.

divergences.reason: the oracle accepts ANY non-empty string as a handle
divergences.rationale: The exporter stubs resolve_handle at the 'non-empty string' gate ONLY (registry liveness is not modelled), so 'abc' passes. Zod requires an explicit store pointer, a bare store:// uri, or a handle of the shape registry_put ACTUALLY produces (`h_<counter>_<8>`). HERE ZOD IS CLOSER TO THE LIVE ENGINE than the oracle is: the real resolve_handle calls registry_get, which fails on an unknown handle.
the engine reads only pointer_uri/format/sidecar and ignores the rest. StorePointer is a `strictObject`, so that a typo ('sidcar') becomes an error instead of a silently lost sidecar.

`{format, sidecar}` without `pointer_uri` is not a pointer as far as the pointer predicate is concerned, and the oracle lets it through. Zod requires `pointer_uri` — without it there is nothing to read from the store.

divergences.reason: the input_example ITSELF contains explicit nulls
divergences.rationale: `mcp_synth_example()` for crps_learning puts `soft_threshold: null` / `hard_threshold: null` and similar on OPTIONAL arguments. The same class as */explicit-null, but inside the example's own base — which is why it is enumerated separately (the example is GENERATED; the worker does not construct it).

divergences.reason: a bare string or an empty array satisfies an ARRAY-of-handles socket
divergences.rationale: TWO known mechanisms COMPOSE here, which is why this class is separate rather than split between `*_array/scalar-or-empty` and `handle/non-conforming-string`. (1) The frozen contract's coercion step FLATTENS "abc" into a length-1 vector — the array nature of the socket is lost BEFORE anything is checked. (2) Then the oracle's stubbed handle resolver keeps ONLY the 'non-empty string' gate, so "abc" passes as a handle. `empty-array` is the same first mechanism at the other extreme: an empty list flattens to nothing and mapping over nothing yields an empty list. The typed schema requires an array of at least two handles: an array socket means an array socket, and the minimum of two mirrors the engine's own DCC specification-list gate, which requires at least two specifications — a single-asset DCC does not exist. The strictness HERE is what matters: a divergence on this socket does not cost one 422, it costs one store read PER asset before it fails.
